title: Local bounded models with finite constant graded terms
statement: Let C be a small site with final object X [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], B a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and K in its derived category of B-module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let integers a<b satisfy H^q(K)=0 outside [a,b] [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and assume that every H^q(K) is locally a constant sheaf of a finitely generated B-module [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. There is a covering {U_i -> X} and, on each slice C/U_i [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], a cochain complex P_i, a family of finite B-modules M_i^q vanishing outside [a,b], isomorphisms P_i^q = constant(M_i^q) for all q, and a derived isomorphism K|U_i = Q(P_i). The differentials of P_i are arbitrary sheaf morphisms; they are not required to be induced by module maps.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, proof of the strengthened bounded constant-model assertion

proof.text: Induct on b-a, simultaneously on all localized sites. Exact restriction preserves cohomology and distinguished triangles [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; restriction of a constant sheaf is constant [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction]. Successive covering refinements compose [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For width zero, concentration identifies K with its sole cohomology sheaf placed in that degree [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single], which is trivialized by the hypothesis. Empty slices have only zero sheaves and admit the zero graded model.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, proof of the strengthened bounded constant-model assertion

proof.text: For positive width, trivialize the finite top cohomology H^b(K)=constant(M). Choose a finite free surjection B^r -> M and a representative complex upper truncated at b [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends]. The cycles-to-homology projection is an epimorphism of module-valued sheaves. Apply the proved local finite-free lifting theorem [lem-weil-pbc-local-finite-free-epi-lift] to lift the induced map from the constant B^r to top cohomology across this epimorphism on a covering. Composing the lifted map with the cycle inclusion gives a chain map from the constant B^r in degree b to the representative, with the prescribed surjective top homology map. This uses the categorical epimorphism directly and needs no separate presheaf quotient identification.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, lifting finite top-cohomology generators (the source omits the details)

proof.text: Form its cone L and distinguished triangle F[-b] -> K -> L -> F[-b+1] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives cohomology bounds [a,b-1], the original cohomology below b-1, and an extension of H^(b-1)(K) by the kernel of the finite-free surjection in degree b-1. The finite locally constant Serre property [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-derived-serre], with Noetherianity, supplies locally constant finite cohomology for L. Apply the induction hypothesis to obtain a bounded sheaf complex E with finite constant graded terms for L.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, proof of the strengthened bounded constant-model assertion

proof.text: Set n=b-1. The bounded sheaf model E of L has zero terms above n, and the boundary is a derived morphism Q(E) -> F[-n]. Apply the proved chain-representative theorem [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-top-chain-representative] to obtain an actual chain map E -> F[-n] representing it. Its degree-n component kills the preceding differential by the chain-map identity. This works for arbitrary finite graded terms: no projectivity or descent of this sheaf morphism to a coefficient-module map is required.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, construction of the final differential from the derived boundary

proof.text: Append F in degree b by taking the shifted cone of this boundary. Its graded terms are the old constant finite terms and the constant finite free term F; the support is [a,b]. Rotation and the morphism-of-triangles axiom [def-weil-triangulated-category] give a comparison with K which is the identity on the other two triangle objects. The long exact cohomology sequences [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] imply that comparison is a quasi-isomorphism, hence an isomorphism after localization. Compose all covering refinements [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The conclusion concerns constant graded terms only, so the final differential-descent part of Tag 094G is deliberately not invoked.

Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/AlternatingConst and Factorizations/CM5a concern different meanings of constant; no constant graded local model theorem.

theorem exists_site_bounded_constant_graded_model
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    (J : Precoverage C) [J.HasIsos] [J.IsStableUnderComposition]
    [J.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [J.HasPullbacks]
    (X : C) (hX : IsTerminal X)
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (ModuleCat.{u} B))]
    [∀ U : C, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (Sheaf (J.toGrothendieck.over U) (ModuleCat.{u} B))]
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (ModuleCat.{u} B)))
    (a b : ℤ) (hab : a < b)
    (hvan : ∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q → IsZero
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (ModuleCat.{u} B)) q).obj K))
    (hloc : ∀ (q : ℤ) (V : C),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → C) (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ V),
        Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J V ∧
        ∀ i : I, ∃ M : ModuleCat.{u} B, Module.Finite B M ∧ Nonempty
          ((J.toGrothendieck.overPullback (ModuleCat.{u} B) (U i)).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
              (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (ModuleCat.{u} B)) q).obj K) ≅
            (constantSheaf (J.toGrothendieck.over (U i)) (ModuleCat.{u} B)).obj M)) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → C) (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ X),
      Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J X ∧
      ∀ i : I, ∃ P : CochainComplex
          (Sheaf (J.toGrothendieck.over (U i)) (ModuleCat.{u} B)) ℤ,
        ∃ M : ℤ → ModuleCat.{u} B,
          (∀ q : ℤ, Module.Finite B (M q)) ∧
          (∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q → IsZero (M q)) ∧
          (∀ q : ℤ, Nonempty (P.X q ≅
            (constantSheaf (J.toGrothendieck.over (U i)) (ModuleCat.{u} B)).obj (M q))) ∧
          Nonempty
            ((@Functor.mapDerivedCategory _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _
                (J.toGrothendieck.overPullback (ModuleCat.{u} B) (U i))
                (Functor.additive_of_preserves_binary_products _) _
                ⟨fun _ _ _ ↦ PreservesColimitsOfSize.preservesColimitsOfShape
                  (self := Adjunction.leftAdjoint_preservesColimits
                    (Functor.sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous
                      (Over.forget (U i)) (ModuleCat.{u} B)
                      (J.toGrothendieck.over (U i)) J.toGrothendieck))⟩).obj K ≅
              DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)

split_report.summary: The cohomological induction part of Tag 094G is separated from the finite simultaneous differential-descent argument, which is proved in Lean. The only remaining hole is this graded construction. The derived boundary chain representative is proved separately using the canonical t-structure, removing the two fraction nodes from this route. Finite-free local lifting across an epimorphism is also proved, so the cycles-to-homology epimorphism can be used directly without the presheaf-quotient detour.

tool_uses.why: Exact restriction is a generic tool for transporting the induction between localized sites; it does not replace the unit route.
The generic long exact homology sequence controls the cone of the locally surjective top-degree map.
